transcript.content:
<issue>
[Bug]: `import.meta.webpackHot?.dispose(...)` compiles to `undefined(...)` (runtime TypeError) when HMR is disabled
### System Info

- Rspack: reproduced on 2.1.2 (latest), 2.0.6, and 1.7.12 - present in both major versions
- webpack 5.108.3 compiles the same input correctly (for comparison)
- Node.js 24.15.0, macOS (darwin arm64)
- No loaders, no plugins needed to reproduce

### Details

When HMR is not enabled (production mode, or development without `HotModuleReplacementPlugin`), Rspack replaces `import.meta.webpackHot` member chains with `undefined`. When the access uses optional chaining followed by a call, the replacement eats the callee but **keeps the call**, producing code that throws `TypeError: undefined is not a function` at module evaluation time.

Input (`src/index.js`, entire file):

```js
import.meta.webpackHot?.dispose(() => console.log('bye'));
console.log('hello');
```

Config (`rspack.config.mjs`, entire file):

```js
export default {
  mode: 'production',
  entry: './src/index.js',
  optimization: { minimize: false },
};
```

Actual output (module body):

```js
undefined(() => console.log('bye'));
console.log('hello');
```

The bundle throws on the first line; `console.log('hello')` is never reached. With `minimize: true` the broken call survives as `(void 0)(...)`.

Expected - what webpack 5.108.3 emits for the identical input/config:

```js
 undefined;
console.log('hello');
```

i.e. the whole optional call expression short-circuits away and the rest of the module runs.

Notes from narrowing it down:

- Not specific to `webpackHot`: any `import.meta.<member>?.method(...)` miscompiles the same way (tested with a made-up member name).
- Not specific to production: `mode: 'development'` without `HotModuleReplacementPlugin` produces the same `undefined(...)`.
- The plain member form without `?.` is handled correctly: `if (import.meta.webpackHot) { import.meta.webpackHot.dispose(cb); }` compiles away cleanly (this is the workaround we use).
- Optional chaining on ordinary runtime values is unaffected; the bug is only in the static `import.meta.*` replacement.

Impact: `import.meta.webpackHot?.dispose(...)` / `?.accept(...)` is the common idiom for HMR cleanup in ESM code (the ESM counterpart of `module.hot?.dispose(...)`). Any module using it crashes the production bundle at module scope

### Reproduce link

https://github.com/Zycon42/rspack-webpackhot-repro

### Reproduce Steps

1. `git clone https://github.com/Zycon42/rspack-webpackhot-repro && cd rspack-webpackhot-repro`
2. `npm install`
3. `npm test` (runs `rspack build && node dist/main.js`)
4. The build output `dist/main.js` contains `undefined(() => console.log('bye'));` and running it throws `TypeError: undefined is not a function`; `hello` is never printed.


</issue>

The repository is at /testbed.

input.instruction: In /testbed (rspack, Rust), find the code handling `import.meta.webpackHot` / import.meta member chain replacement with `undefined` (likely crates/rspack_plugin_javascript/src/parser_plugin/import_meta_plugin.rs or similar, `members_optionals`/`call_member_chain` hooks). Also find how the module.hot / `module.hot?.accept` handling does it (api_plugin / hmr plugin) and how optional call handling is done in the parser (e.g. `optional_chaining` / `ExprOrSpread` ... `CallExpression` with optional chain). Report file paths, line numbers and the relevant code verbatim.

content.content: {"summary":"I found no `webpackHot` string in `rspack_plugin_javascript/src`. The code that replaces `import.meta` member chains with `undefined` is in `import_meta_plugin.rs`. `import.meta.webpackHot` is handled in `hot_module_replacement_plugin.rs` through `expr_name::IMPORT_META_HOT` and `ImportMetaKnownProperties::WEBPACK_HOT`. Optional chains are walked by `walk_chain_expression` and `enter_optional_chain`.","findings":["crates/rspack_plugin_javascript/src/parser_plugin/import_meta_plugin.rs:~795-832 is the `member` hook for the `import.meta` root (`root == expr_name::IMPORT_META`). It calls `get_member_expression_info(ExprRef::Member(expr), AllowedMemberTypes::Expression)`. It returns early if `PreserveUnknown` is set or `preserve_property(members.members.first())` is true. If `members.members.get(1).is_some() && members.members_optionals.get(1).is_some_and(|o| *o)`, it emits `ConstDependency::new(expr.span().into(), \"undefined\".into())`. Otherwise it emits `import_meta_unknown_property(members)`. If no member info is found, it also emits `\"undefined\"`. The dependency goes through `parser.add_presentational_dependency` and the hook returns `Some(true)`.","import_meta_plugin.rs:274 `skip_undefined_evaluation` and lines ~516-573 (`evaluated = Some(\"undefined\")`, `eval::evaluate_to_undefined(span.real_lo(), span.real_hi())`) handle evaluating unknown `import.meta` properties to undefined. Line ~358 contains the `\" */ undefined\"` string.","crates/rspack_plugin_javascript/src/parser_plugin/hot_module_replacement_plugin.rs:~205-285 defines `ImportMetaHotReplacementParserPlugin`. Its `evaluate_identifier`, `member` and `call` hooks match `expr_name::IMPORT_META_HOT`, `IMPORT_META_HOT_ACCEPT` and `IMPORT_META_HOT_DECLINE`. Each is gated by `parser.javascript_options.import_meta().is_known_property_enabled(ImportMetaKnownProperties::WEBPACK_HOT)`. `member` calls `parser.create_hmr_expression_handler(expr.span())` and returns `Some(true)`. `call` runs `create_accept_handler` or `create_decline_handler` with `ImportMetaHotAcceptDependency` or `ImportMetaHotDeclineDependency`.","hot_module_replacement_plugin.rs:~129-195 defines `ModuleHotReplacementParserPlugin` for `module.hot`. It uses `expr_name::MODULE_HOT`, `MODULE_HOT_ACCEPT` and `MODULE_HOT_DECLINE`. It has the same `evaluate_identifier`, `member` and `call` structure, with `ModuleHotAcceptDependency` and `ModuleHotDeclineDependency`.","hot_module_replacement_plugin.rs:51 `create_hmr_expression_handler(span)` sets `build_info.module_concatenation_bailout = Some(\"Hot Module Replacement\")`. It then adds a `ModuleArgumentDependency::new(Some(\"hot\".into()), span.into(), loc)`. `create_accept_handler` is at line 62 and `create_decline_handler` at line 103. `extract_deps` is at line 19.","`members_optionals` hooks: the trait hooks `member_chain` and `call_member_chain` are dispatched in parser_plugin/drive.rs:~191 and ~211. The `call_member_chain` implementations are in api_plugin.rs:689, common_js_imports_parse_plugin.rs:2167, worker_plugin.rs:404, esm_import_dependency_parser_plugin.rs:314, import_parser_plugin.rs:228 and common_js_exports_parse_plugin.rs:505. They call `get_non_optional_part(members, members_optionals)`. `api_plugin.rs` ignores `_members_optionals`.","Optional-chain handling in the parser: visitors/dependency/parser/walk.rs:1149 `walk_chain_expression` first calls `plugin_drive.optional_chaining(self, expr)`. If that returns `None`, it calls `self.enter_optional_chain(expr, |p, call| p.walk_opt_call(call), |p, member| p.walk_member_expression(member))`. `walk.rs:572` dispatches `Expr::OptChain` to it.","visitors/dependency/parser/mod.rs:1324 `enter_optional_chain` saves `member_expr_in_optional_chain`. For `OptChainBase::Call`, it sets the flag to `expr.optional` only if `call.callee.is_member()`. For `OptChainBase::Member`, it sets the flag to `expr.optional`. It then runs the callback and restores the flag. The OptChain handling in `get_member_expression_info` is around mod.rs:1209-1211, and mod.rs:1517 has a second `enter_optional_chain` call. `call_hooks_name.rs:120` implements `CallHooksName` for `OptChainExpr`."],"confidence":0.8}
